name: Langerhans Cell Sarcoma

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Histopathological and Immunophenotypic Diagnostic Criteria for Langerhans Cell Sarcoma

criteria.description: Presence of malignant Langerhans cells with cytologic atypia and high mitotic activity on histopathology
Positive immunohistochemical staining for CD1a, langerin (CD207), and S100 protein
Identification of Birbeck granules on electron microscopy (if available)
Exclusion of other histiocytic and dendritic cell neoplasms

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological evidence of malignant Langerhans cells with positive immunophenotyping for CD1a, langerin, and S100, plus exclusion of other neoplasms
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Electron microscopy is supportive but not mandatory; diagnosis relies heavily on immunohistochemical profile and morphology.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Cutaneous ulcerative nodules with malignant Langerhans cell infiltration
pathognomonic.notes: Characteristic skin lesions often present at diagnosis

pathognomonic.symptomName: Lymphadenopathy with malignant Langerhans cell involvement
pathognomonic.notes: Enlarged lymph nodes due to tumor infiltration
searchTerms: swollen lymph nodes with cancer cells

common.symptomName: Bone pain due to osseous lesions
common.notes: Commonly affected sites include skull and long bones
searchTerms: aching bones due to bone damage

common.notes: May be related to systemic inflammatory response

searchTerms: unintentional weight loss and poor appetite

common.notes: Involvement of liver and spleen by malignant cells

occasional.notes: May present with cough or dyspnea

occasional.symptomName: Neurological deficits due to CNS involvement
occasional.notes: Rare but possible central nervous system infiltration
searchTerms: neurological signs due to CNS disease

occasional.symptomName: Anemia secondary to bone marrow involvement
searchTerms: low red blood cells from marrow disease
anemia due to bone marrow problems

rare.symptomName: Endocrine dysfunction due to hypothalamic-pituitary axis involvement
rare.notes: May cause diabetes insipidus or other hormonal abnormalities
searchTerms: hormone problems from brain area damage

rare.symptomName: Cardiovascular compromise from mediastinal mass effect
searchTerms: heart and vessel problems from chest mass
cardiovascular issues due to mediastinal pressure
renal dysfunction due to tissue infiltration

laboratory: Anemia and thrombocytopenia in peripheral blood
imaging: Lytic bone lesions on X-ray or CT
Pulmonary nodules or infiltrates on chest CT
genetic: No consistent recurrent genetic mutations identified
Occasional BRAF V600E mutation reported in some cases
other: Histopathology showing malignant Langerhans cells with nuclear atypia
Immunohistochemistry positive for CD1a, langerin (CD207), and S100 protein
Electron microscopy demonstrating Birbeck granules (if performed)

distinguishingFeatures: Benign or intermediate histology without overt cytologic atypia
ALK gene rearrangements in some cases

redFlags: Rapidly enlarging cutaneous or nodal masses
Unexplained lytic bone lesions with systemic symptoms
references: Swerdlow SH, Campo E, Harris NL, et al. WHO Classification of Tumours of Haematopoietic and Lymphoid Tissues. IARC; 2017.
Feldman AL, Arber DA. Langerhans cell sarcoma: a review and update. Adv Anat Pathol. 2014;21(3):161-167.
